title: T3 Code UI overhaul (example)
goal: Make T3 Code's UI look as if it had a full-time designer, then score higher than Claude Code and Codex.
provenance: ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION, not affiliated with or checked by the video's author. Based on the narration of 'Agents Sucked At UI (Until Today)', Theo (t3.gg), YouTube xq0eB8vxeqk, 3 Nov 2026, read from its transcript. Scores are as heard and approximate; round boundaries after round 3 are approximate. No screenshots or exact changes were available, so evidence is notes only.

target.rule: every council judge scores the screenshots ≥ 9 (later raised to 9.5, then 10)

budget.cost: about $250 for the work shown (list-price estimate; mostly subscriptions)

human_signal.text: Critique of the fonts, border radius, icons and font hierarchy
human_signal.source: user critique on X that started the run

human_signal.text: Should score higher than the two competitor apps in every ranking
human_signal.source: owner follow-up, phase 2, with Claude Code and Codex screenshots

rubric.overall: judge holistic score of the screenshot set

criteria.name: Hierarchy
criteria.description: What the eye lands on first; sidebar receding behind content

criteria.name: Typography
criteria.description: Fonts, fallback font, size and weight scale

criteria.name: Colour and contrast
criteria.description: Readable body text in light mode; colour where it carries meaning

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.description: Same label, radius and indicator for the same thing across surfaces

changes.what: Comparators added to the judging panel (Claude Code, Codex screenshots); fresh context
changes.why: Owner judged the 9/10 result not good enough next to competitors

agents.name: Orchestrator
agents.notes: Ran the judge panel each round

agents.name: Builder
agents.notes: Made the UI changes and before/after diagrams

agents.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
agents.notes: Fastest judge; used alone until it reached the threshold in phase 2

rounds.summary: Phase 1. Scores after the first batch.

evidence.text: Changes not itemised in the source.

rounds.summary: Phase 1 target met: every judge 9. Owner compared the app with Claude Code and ChatGPT by eye and judged it still not good enough.

decisions.decision: Start a fresh thread with competitor screenshots in the judging panel
decisions.reason: Scores in isolation were higher than the owner's own comparison

rounds.summary: Phase 2, fresh context, comparators in the panel. The same PR that scored 9 in phase 1 now scores 7.4 from Sol.

judge_notes.text: Rated one comparator's UI as unclear.

decisions.decision: Stage the judges: Sol alone until it reaches the threshold, then Opus, then Muse
decisions.reason: Muse usage running out; slow judges delaying rounds

rounds.summary: Sol and Opus both 9; Muse 7.9, then usage ran out. Changes across phase 2: consistent labels across surfaces, calmer sidebar colour and text hierarchy, consistent radius, fonts and indicators, better body contrast in light mode.

decisions.decision: Fork a worktree and raise the target to 9.5 in every category

evidence.text: Phase 3 took 10 more rounds; collapsed into round 10 here.

rounds.summary: Phase 3 end (10 iterations collapsed). Every judge rated every category ≥ 9.5 by the last iteration; Opus's overall was 9.3. Comparator screenshots never changed, yet their scores rose.

judge_notes.text: Owner suspects stating the 9.5 target to judges inflated scores; next time hide it.

decisions.decision: Run a 10/10 branch with an added colour preference

evidence.text: Owner on the 10/10 result: merge reads clearly as a button, icons more visible, light-mode syntax far more readable.

outcome.verdict: Every judge ≥ 9.5 in every category (phase 3); later 10/10 from Sol and Muse
outcome.owner_verdict: "This objectively just feels better than it was before." Shipped behind a beta toggle.
outcome.notes: Lessons the source draws: programmatic scores beat judge scores where available; comparators change judges' scores; hide the target from judges.
later: Make the UI work on a small screen
